purpose: Short welcome and teaching samples requested by Arthur; approximately 6–10 seconds each.

clips.text: Welcome to English. Crept and strode both describe movement, but they suggest very different feelings.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to math. Double an input, then add three. Increasing the input by one increases the output by two.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to science. Seeing brown spots is an observation. Explaining their cause takes evidence.
clips.previous_text: Welcome to science. Brown spots are an observation. Their cause is an explanation we still need to test.
clips.revision_reason: Make the observation/explanation distinction precise and concrete.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to history. Before trusting an account, ask who created it, and what they could actually know.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to geography. Map scale connects a distance on the page to a distance on the ground.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: And contour lines show elevation. When their spacing gets closer, the slope gets steeper.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to Language Arts. Your audience shapes your words. A friendly message sounds different from a formal request.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to health. A popular claim is not proof. Check its source and the evidence behind it.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to physical education. Different exercises train different skills. Today, we'll connect each exercise to its purpose.
clips.previous_text: Welcome to P.E. Training should fit your goal. What you practice shapes the skills you develop.
clips.revision_reason: Spell out physical education and replace the unclear line flagged by Arthur.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to art. A light shape against a dark background stands out. That difference is called contrast.
clips.previous_text: Welcome to art. Contrast directs attention. Change one value, and watch how the focal point shifts.
clips.revision_reason: Replace unexplained value and focal-point terminology with a visible example.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to music. Pitch tells us how high a sound is; timbre gives it its distinctive character.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to drama. The same words can express different intentions. Listen to how emphasis changes a line.
clips.previous_text: Welcome to drama. You came back. The words stay the same; the intention changes how we say them.
clips.revision_reason: Replace the abrupt unexplained quotation with a clear teaching introduction.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to technology. An algorithm is an ordered set of instructions. Change the order, and the result can change.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.

clips.text: Welcome to our school. Make a claim, show your evidence, and explain how the two connect.
clips.verification: Script reviewed; spoken wording checked by local transcription.
